English: What digital evidence is
What is it?

Digital evidence is any record that helps establish what happened: chats, call logs, bank messages and statements, emails, web addresses (URLs), profile IDs, app details, photos of a screen, and device information. Collect the minimum evidence the agencies need to act — enough to identify the transaction, the account and the suspect identifiers — without delaying help. Safety and live loss always come before evidence capture.

Native record and working copy
What is it?

The native record is the original item where it lives — the chat inside WhatsApp, the email in the mailbox, the transaction in the bank's system. A working copy is a screenshot, export or download made from it. Copies are useful, but the original must stay untouched so that the police can collect it properly later.

Time, time zones and metadata
What is it?

Every item has at least three times: when it happened, when it was captured, and when it was transferred. Confusing them is one of the commonest reasons complaints are delayed. Always write the date, the time and “IST”. Metadata is “data about data”: when a file was created, by which device, sometimes where. Social media and messaging apps often strip or change metadata, which is another reason to keep the native record and to note times yourself.

Evidence register and chain of custody
What is it?

The evidence register is a simple table with one row per item. The chain of custody is the record of every person who has held the item, when and why. Together they let anyone check that the evidence is complete and has not been tampered with.

Integrity hashing with SHA-256
What is it?

A hash is a fixed-length “fingerprint” calculated from a file. SHA-256 is a widely used hash method. If even one dot of the file changes, the hash changes completely. Recording the hash of the master copy lets anyone later show that a working copy is identical.

Hash the master once, record it, and never open the master for editing. Compare hashes whenever a copy changes hands.
Safeguarding, the law and your role
What is it?

Some evidence is itself harmful. Copying or forwarding intimate images re-victimises the person, and possessing or sharing child sexual abuse material is a serious offence even when the intention is to help. For such material the First Responder preserves only identifiers — links, usernames, platform and time — and reports.

The preservation boundary
In the role: advise the citizen not to delete; capture working copies of what the citizen shows you, with consent; register, hash and hand over.
Outside the role: unlocking or taking the device, forensic imaging, recovering deleted data, accessing the suspect's accounts, analysing malware. Refer these to the police or the IT lead.
